course.title: Full-Stack Web Development
course.description: Build complete web applications from frontend through backend, databases and APIs to deployment. Progressive path from HTML/CSS fundamentals to a deployed full-stack project.

modules.title: Module 1: Frontend development
modules.description: HTML, CSS, JavaScript and responsive UI.

lessons.title: Lesson 1.1: HTML and CSS
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Build semantic HTML pages and style them with modern CSS including layout techniques.

lessons.title: Lesson 1.2: JavaScript fundamentals
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Write JavaScript that responds to user events and updates the page.

lessons.title: Lesson 1.3: Responsive, user-friendly interfaces
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Apply responsive design so layouts adapt across screen sizes and remain usable.

lessons.title: Module 1 review and assessment
lessons.notesHtml:
Module 1 review and assessment

10 questions. Pass mark 70 %.
lessons.quiz:
Q: HTML primarily provides:
Styling only
*Document structure and meaning
Server logic
Database queries
explain: Structure and semantics.
level: 1

Q: CSS is used for:
Database design
*Presentation and layout
Server authentication
Only animations forever
explain: Look and layout.
level: 1

Q: JavaScript in the browser enables:
Only static pages
*Interactivity and dynamic updates
Only server-side rendering
Replacing HTML entirely always
explain: Client-side behaviour.
level: 1

Q: Responsive design means:
Only desktop layouts
*Interfaces that adapt usefully across device sizes
Fixed pixel widths only
Ignoring mobile users
explain: Multi-device usability.
level: 1

Q: Semantic HTML helps:
Only search engines never users
*Accessibility, maintainability and often SEO
Only make pages slower
Replace CSS
explain: Meaning aids tools and people.
level: 2

Q: Event listeners in JavaScript:
Only run on the server
*Respond to user actions such as clicks and form submits
Delete the DOM always
Replace HTML structure
explain: Reaction to events.
level: 1

Q: Flexbox and Grid are:
Database indexes
*CSS layout systems
JavaScript frameworks only
HTTP methods
explain: Modern layout tools.
level: 2

Q: Accessibility considerations include:
Only colour choices for decoration
*Keyboard use, contrast, labels and semantic structure
Ignoring screen readers
Tiny touch targets
explain: Inclusive design.
level: 2

Q: A form should:
Have no labels
*Use proper labels, validation and clear error messages
Submit without feedback
Only work on desktop
explain: Usable forms.
level: 1

Q: Frontend quality is judged by:
Only lines of code
*Usability, accessibility, performance and maintainability on real devices
Only how new the framework is
Server logs only
explain: User-centred quality.
level: 1

lessons.title: Lesson 2.1: How servers and requests work
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Explain the request-response cycle and implement simple routes that return data.

lessons.title: Lesson 2.2: Server-side programming
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Organise server code into routes, services and clear error handling.

lessons.title: Lesson 2.3: Authentication and security basics
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Implement basic authentication flows and apply fundamental security practices.

lessons.title: Module 2 review and assessment
lessons.notesHtml:
Module 2 review and assessment

10 questions. Pass mark 70 %.
lessons.quiz:
Q: HTTP is primarily:
A database language
*A request-response protocol for the web
A CSS framework
A password manager
explain: Web protocol.
level: 1

Q: A route maps:
Only CSS files
*A URL pattern and method to handler logic
Only images
Databases to spreadsheets
explain: Routing.
level: 1

Q: Server-side code is trusted more than client code because:
It runs in the user’s browser
*It runs in an environment you control; clients can be modified by users
It never has bugs
It cannot access databases
explain: Trust boundary.
level: 2

Q: Authentication establishes:
Authorisation policies only
*Who the user is
Only the colour theme
Network latency
explain: Identity.
level: 1

Q: Authorisation decides:
Who the user is
*What an authenticated user is allowed to do
Only password strength
DNS records
explain: Permissions.
level: 1

Q: Storing passwords should use:
Plain text
*Strong one-way hashing with modern algorithms and salts
Reversible encryption only
The same hash for everyone
explain: Hashing best practice.
level: 2

Q: HTTPS protects:
Only images
*Data in transit from eavesdropping and tampering
Only server disk
Nothing useful
explain: Transport security.
level: 1

Q: Input validation on the server is:
Optional if the frontend validates
*Required because clients can bypass frontend checks
Only for numbers
A replacement for authentication
explain: Never trust the client.
level: 1

Q: Sessions or tokens are used to:
Style pages
*Maintain login state across requests
Compile CSS
Replace databases
explain: Stateful identity across HTTP.
level: 2

Q: Security defaults should favour:
Convenience over safety always
*Safe configurations that developers must consciously relax if needed
Open admin panels
Shared passwords
explain: Secure by default.
level: 2

lessons.title: Lesson 3.1: Database design
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Design a simple relational schema with primary and foreign keys.

lessons.title: Lesson 3.2: Storing and retrieving data
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Perform create, read, update and delete operations safely from application code.

lessons.title: Lesson 3.3: Connecting an application to a database
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Connect a backend service to a database with sensible configuration and migration discipline.

lessons.title: Module 3 review and assessment
lessons.notesHtml:
Module 3 review and assessment

10 questions. Pass mark 70 %.
lessons.quiz:
Q: A primary key uniquely identifies:
Only columns
*Each row in a table
Only the database name
HTTP methods
explain: Row identity.
level: 1

Q: A foreign key references:
A CSS class
*A primary key in another (or the same) table
Only indexes
Passwords
explain: Relationships.
level: 1

Q: CRUD stands for:
Compile, Run, Update, Deploy
*Create, Read, Update, Delete
: Core data operations.
level: 1

Q: Parameterised queries help prevent:
Slow networks
*SQL injection
CSS bugs
Missing images
explain: Safe query construction.
level: 1

Q: Normalisation aims to:
Duplicate data everywhere
*Reduce redundant data and update anomalies
Slow all queries
Eliminate all relationships
explain: Clean relational design.
level: 2

Q: Migrations help teams:
Avoid version control
*Evolve schema in a controlled, repeatable way
Delete all data weekly
Ignore production
explain: Controlled schema change.
level: 2

Q: Connection pooling is used to:
Open a new TCP connection for every query without reuse
*Reuse database connections efficiently
Replace the database
Store passwords in URLs
explain: Efficient connection use.
level: 2

Q: Indexes speed up:
All writes always
*Many read queries at the cost of some write overhead and storage
Only backups
CSS rendering
explain: Read optimisation trade-off.
level: 2

Q: Backing up databases is:
Optional for production
*Essential for recovery from failure or mistakes
Only for development
Replaced by replication alone always
explain: Recovery insurance.
level: 1

Q: Application code should:
Embed database admin passwords in frontend JS
*Keep credentials and direct DB access on the server side
Allow any client to run arbitrary SQL
Skip error handling
explain: Trust boundary again.
level: 1

lessons.title: Lesson 4.1: Designing and building APIs
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Design a small REST-style API with clear resources and correct HTTP semantics.

lessons.title: Lesson 4.2: Using third-party APIs
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Integrate an external API with proper error handling and secret management.

lessons.title: Lesson 4.3: Joining frontend and backend
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Connect a frontend UI to your backend API end-to-end.

lessons.title: Module 4 review and assessment
lessons.notesHtml:
Module 4 review and assessment

10 questions. Pass mark 70 %.
lessons.quiz:
Q: REST-style APIs often model:
Only files on disk
*Resources accessed via HTTP methods
Only WebSocket streams
CSS rules
explain: Resource + method.
level: 1

Q: HTTP status 404 means:
Success
*Not found
Server error
Redirect
explain: Resource missing.
level: 1

Q: HTTP status 401/403 relate to:
Caching only
*Authentication / authorisation problems
Successful creation
Static files
explain: Access control statuses.
level: 2

Q: API keys and secrets should be:
Committed to public repos
*Kept in environment/config not in client-side code
Shared in screenshots
Embedded in CSS
explain: Secret hygiene.
level: 1

Q: Rate limits exist to:
Speed up all clients infinitely
*Protect services from overload and abuse
Disable security
Replace authentication
explain: Protection mechanism.
level: 2

Q: Idempotent methods (like GET, PUT in careful design) help because:
They always change state twice
*Repeating the request does not cause unintended extra effects
They are slower
They ignore authentication
explain: Safe retries.
level: 2

Q: CORS policies control:
Database colours
*Which web origins may call your API from browsers
Database indexes
DNS only
explain: Browser same-origin policy extensions.
level: 2

Q: Validating API input on the server is:
Redundant if the client validates
*Required
Only for integers
Optional in production
explain: Never trust clients.
level: 1

Q: Versioning APIs helps:
Break all clients immediately
*Evolve contracts without surprising existing consumers
Hide documentation
Avoid status codes
explain: Controlled evolution.
level: 2

Q: End-to-end integration means:
Only unit tests
*Frontend and backend working together for real user flows
Only database migrations
Only CI configuration
explain: Full path works.
level: 1

modules.title: Module 5: Deployment and projects
modules.description: Test, deploy and ship a complete application.

lessons.title: Lesson 5.1: Testing and debugging
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Apply basic automated tests and systematic debugging techniques.

lessons.title: Lesson 5.2: Deploying a web application
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Deploy an application to a hosting platform with environment configuration and HTTPS.

lessons.title: Lesson 5.3: Final practical web development project
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Deliver a small full-stack application that demonstrates the full course skill set.

lessons.title: Module 5 review and assessment
lessons.notesHtml:
Module 5 review and assessment

10 questions. Pass mark 70 %.
lessons.quiz:
Q: Automated tests help by:
Replacing all manual checks forever
*Catching regressions quickly when code changes
Slowing development with no benefit
Only testing the database
explain: Fast safety net.
level: 1

Q: Debugging effectively usually starts with:
Rewriting everything
*Reproducing the issue and gathering evidence (logs, errors, inputs)
Blaming the framework
Disabling all logging
explain: Reproduce + observe.
level: 1

Q: Environment variables are used in deployment to:
Hard-code secrets in source
*Configure secrets and settings without hard-coding them in source
Style the UI
Replace HTTPS
explain: Config vs code.
level: 1

Q: HTTPS in production is:
Optional decoration
*Expected for protecting users and enabling modern web features
Only for banks
Replaced by HTTP/2 alone
explain: Baseline security.
level: 1

Q: A production deployment checklist often includes:
Only the happy path on localhost
*Build, config, migrations, health checks, monitoring and rollback plan
Deleting all logs
Sharing admin passwords in chat
explain: Operational readiness.
level: 2

Q: Monitoring after deploy helps:
Ignore failures
*Detect errors and performance issues in real use
Replace testing
Avoid user feedback
explain: Observability.
level: 2

Q: A good course project demonstrates:
Only one HTML file
*Frontend, backend, data storage, and deployment of a coherent user-facing app
Only a README
Only a design mockup
explain: End-to-end skill.
level: 1

Q: Rollbacks matter because:
Deploys never fail
*New releases can introduce critical bugs; quick recovery limits harm
They slow learning
They are only for databases
explain: Recovery path.
level: 2

Q: Logging in production should:
Include every password
*Help diagnose issues without leaking secrets
Be turned off completely
Only exist on developer machines
explain: Useful + safe logs.
level: 2

Q: The aim of full-stack training is to:
Memorise every framework
*Build, connect and operate complete web applications that solve real problems
Only write CSS
Avoid all databases
explain: Complete working systems.
level: 1
